claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility.

Are you responsible for Alex? This usually means he lives with you, or you contribute towards the cost of looking after him at least equal to the amount of Child Benefit you would receive.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute towards his upkeep regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex doesn't live with you but you do contribute financially, I have a couple more follow-up questions.

Does someone else also claim Child Benefit for Alex, such as the person he lives with?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Could you tell me a bit more about Alex's living situation? Specifically, who does Alex live with, and why doesn't he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, my ex-partner. We separated a while back and he stayed with her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. I understand Alex lives with his mum following your separation.

One more important question: Is there a reason why Alex's mum isn't claiming Child Benefit for him, even though he lives with her?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure why she hasn't claimed it - she just hasn't got around to it I suppose. But I'm the one who's been contributing money towards his costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me check the specific rules around Child Benefit eligibility when a child lives with someone else.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I've now reviewed the eligibility rules, and I have some important information for you.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 6 years old and lives with his mum (your ex-partner)
- You contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep
- Nobody is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Here's what the rules say:

**Usually, the person the child lives with has priority for Child Benefit.** Since Alex lives with his mum, she would normally be the one expected to claim. However, since she hasn't claimed and you are contributing financially towards Alex's upkeep, you may be eligible.

To confirm your eligibility, I need to check one more thing:

Are your financial contributions towards Alex at least equal to the Child Benefit amount (currently £25.60 per week for an only/eldest child, or approximately £111 per month)? These contributions can be towards things like clothes, food, pocket money, or helping provide somewhere for him to live.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute £30 a week towards his costs - things like clothes, food, and helping out with what he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. £30 per week is above the Child Benefit amount (currently £25.60 per week for a first child), so that's good.

I just have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, no - I don't live in the UK anymore. I moved abroad but I'm still supporting Alex financially.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's an important detail.

Could you tell me which country you moved to? And are you by any chance working for the UK government (as a Crown servant), or do you have any other connection to UK employment or the armed forces?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I just moved abroad for personal reasons but I'm still paying to support Alex back home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I now have enough information to make a determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**UK Residency Requirement:** To qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. While there are some exceptions (such as being a Crown servant or working for the UK government abroad), you've confirmed these don't apply to your situation.

Although you are contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep—which exceeds the Child Benefit amount—this alone is not enough to qualify when you're living abroad without a qualifying exemption.

**What you could consider:**

Since Alex lives with his mum in the UK, she would be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him. It might be worth discussing this with her, as she could make a claim and receive the benefit directly. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, and since she lives with Alex in the UK, she meets the eligibility criteria.

I hope this helps clarify the situation. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
